Re: Standard Appeal — Denial of Prior Authorization for Total Hip Arthroplasty (CPT 27130)
Member: Taylor Ellison
Member ID: W398278970
Reference Number: POC-19407106E9-21880
Date of Notice: 2026-08-02

To the Appeals Review Committee:

I am writing to appeal the adverse benefit determination dated 2026-08-02, which denied prior authorization for a total hip replacement (CPT 27130) for Taylor Ellison on the stated basis that "the requested procedure does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity."

I am submitting this appeal on [date] to ensure it is received well within any applicable filing deadline. I note that the denial notice states an appeal deadline of 180 days from the date of notice, while other Healthy Blue member materials I have reviewed describe a 60-day filing window for Medicaid managed-care appeals. To avoid any question of timeliness, this appeal is being filed within 60 days of the notice date. I ask the plan to confirm in writing which filing deadline applies to this member's coverage.

Request for the specific criteria applied

Before this determination was made, I was not provided with the full text of the medical-necessity criteria the plan applied to CPT 27130 in this member's case. I have not been able to independently verify or quote that criteria language, and I am not attributing any specific wording to the plan in this letter unless noted otherwise. I formally request, pursuant to the member's right to the specific benefit provision, guideline, protocol, or other similar criterion relied upon in making this determination, that Healthy Blue provide:

- The complete text of the medical policy or clinical utilization management guideline applied to this denial (identified in plan materials as the "Hip Arthroplasty" guideline, MCG code S-560 / guideline ID W0105, as customized by the plan's Medical Policy & Technology Assessment Committee), including the edition/version and effective date in force on 2026-08-02; and
- Any plan-specific medical policy document, if different from the MCG guideline, that was applied to this specific request.

I reserve the right to supplement this appeal with a further response addressing the plan's specific criteria once that document is provided.

Clinical basis for medical necessity

Regardless of the precise wording of the plan's criteria, the following documented clinical facts, drawn from the prior authorization packet submitted by Dr. Duval, support that this total hip replacement is medically necessary under generally accepted orthopedic standards for end-stage degenerative hip disease:

1. Chronicity and severity of symptoms: The member has experienced 12 months of progressive hip pain that is unrelieved by rest.

2. Documented failure of conservative (non-surgical) management, including:
   - Supervised physical therapy focused on hip abductor strengthening and gait training, 14 weeks in duration (2026-02-28 through 2026-06-06), with 24 visits completed, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note;
   - NSAID therapy for 8 months with inadequate relief of symptoms; and
   - A corticosteroid injection administered 2026-03-08, which produced only approximately 4 weeks of partial relief before symptoms recurred.

3. Objective imaging confirmation of severe joint disease: A weight-bearing AP pelvis radiograph dated 2026-07-06 shows joint space narrowed to 1 mm superolaterally with subchondral sclerosis and osteophyte formation — findings consistent with advanced degenerative joint disease of the hip.

4. Significant functional impairment: The member currently ambulates with a cane, is limited to walking approximately one block, and cannot put on shoes unassisted — demonstrating substantial loss of function in activities of daily living.

5. Physical examination findings: Positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain, consistent with the radiographic findings above.

6. Absence of contraindications: There is no active infection and no untreated substance use disorder. The member's BMI is 29, and the member is a non-smoker — none of which represent a barrier to surgery.

Taken together, these records reflect a patient with radiographically severe, symptomatic hip degenerative joint disease who has completed and failed an adequate trial of conservative management (structured physical therapy, prolonged NSAID use, and injection therapy) and who has significant, objectively documented functional limitation. In my own words — and without attributing this framing to any specific plan document I have not been given — this clinical picture is the type of presentation that orthopedic and payer medical-necessity standards for total hip arthroplasty are generally intended to cover: chronic pain, imaging-confirmed severe joint space loss, and functional decline unresponsive to non-operative treatment.

Requested action

I ask that Healthy Blue:
1. Reverse the denial and approve the prior authorization request for CPT 27130 (total hip arthroplasty) for Taylor Ellison; and
2. Provide, in writing, the specific medical policy or clinical UM guideline criteria applied to this determination, as requested above, so that this appeal may be supplemented if necessary.

Enclosed with this appeal are copies of:
- The physical therapy discharge note (2026-02-28 to 2026-06-06, 24 visits)
- Medication/injection records documenting 8 months of NSAID use and the 2026-03-08 corticosteroid injection
- The weight-bearing AP pelvis radiograph and radiology report dated 2026-07-06
- Dr. Duval's clinical/exam notes documenting functional limitation and provocative testing
- [Any additional records the provider's office identifies as part of the original PA packet]
